newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Nelson at full output end-Friday - operator.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Nelson at full output end-Friday - operator.

text.p: The North Sea Nelson field will be back to the normal production level of around 140,000 barrels per day by the end of Friday, operator Enterprise Oil said.
Output was cut back last week to allow repairs to a gas dehydration equipment and the field was shut down completely on Tuesday night when a fault in the water system was discovered.
"We've cured the problem," said a spokesman for Enterprise.
"It's started up again but not at full production...current production is about 60,000 bpd," he said.
He said it would take a few hours before the gas compression system would be working at full capacity after a long outage.

Nelson feeds into the Forties stream, and problems at the field over the last week have resulted in the deferral to the August loading programme of about 1.25 million barrels of Forties originally scheduled to load in July.
Maintenance work on a faulty gas compressor took average production at Nelson down to just 25,000 bpd in June.
